threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the tube app like it's a crystal ball; locals know the bus is faster half the time.
Saw a couple on the bus last night arguing over who left the milk out. By the time we hit Stockwell, they had swapped to sharing a bag of chips.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a group of kids argue over which Döner spot had the spiciest sauce, and they were serious about it. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you'll find spontaneous open-air cinema events in parks—projecting classics on blankets under the stars. It's pure Berlin magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows the difference between a BART delay and a BART meltdown. The eye roll when the Civic Center station closed? Classic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters at the Civic Center stop with a ukulele while the bus was delayed. Crowd loved it, even with the chaos around.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume we all drink sangria at the corner bars—most locals prefer a cervecita at home or a quiet vermut in the plaza.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they navigate the metro—still clutching a paper map and fumbling with the ticket machines.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the number 73 bus is a quick way to get to the city—wait till you're stuck behind a school run and the inevitable traffic.
Last night on the 196, a guy was arguing with his reflection in the window, convinced it was a rival. We all just pretended to look out.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh currywurst wafting through the Sunday market, as kids chase pigeons and the old man feeds them from his pocket. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not unusual to find a kebab shop open at 4 AM serving late-night dancers returning from Berghain, a true testament to Berlin's nightlife culture.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they know to avoid the Civic Center BART station after 6 PM—never a good sign when smoke starts billowing.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 31 Balboa, tapping his foot to music only he could hear. Just another Tuesday in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can find authentic Catalan food near the Sagrada Família, but you’ll only get frozen paella and view selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their bright white sneakers. Locals know that a little scuff goes a long way in this city.
